raw.thesis:
Narma proposes an "Enterprise Agentic Brain" for AI-first companies. The core innovation lies in its three-layered architecture: an Observe layer with lightweight desktop sensors for work pattern capture, an Intelligence Layer (the "Brain") to detect employee intent, business value, and "drift," and an Execution Layer (the "Agent Factory") to automatically generate, deploy, and monitor AI agents for validated high-ROI opportunities. This system aims to provide a "Continuous AI lift" by observing work, deciding AI actions, and continuously building agents. Narma focuses on leveraging existing foundation models and creating a "Work Graph" to identify inefficiencies and opportunities for AI intervention.

Narma is designed for AI-first companies that struggle with a lack of telemetry to pinpoint AI savings, unreliable ROI measurements, and constant drift in systems and human resources. By providing a comprehensive system for observing, understanding, and automating work processes with AI, Narma aims to solve the critical problem of scaling AI automation effectively and measurably within these enterprises.

The founder's goal, based on the provided description, appears to be a growth-oriented startup, given the focus on "at scale" deployment and "Continuous AI lift." The venture is currently at the idea stage, as no artifacts or signals like prototypes, users, or revenue are mentioned. There is no information regarding the team beyond the venture name, and no details on founder resources or investment status were provided.
